events.headline: Microsoft's India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad becomes generally available
events.detail: Microsoft announced general availability of its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad, Telangana on August 6, 2026. The region, Microsoft's fourth in India, has three Availability Zones and is backed by Microsoft's $20.5 billion investment commitment to India's cloud and AI future. Early access customers include Adani Group, Bajaj Finserv, HDFC Bank and PB Pay.

events.headline: Koray Kavukcuoglu named SVP to lead Google DeepMind's frontier AI development, replacing Demis Hassabis in that role
events.detail: Koray Kavukcuoglu, DeepMind's former CTO, is becoming head of the unit, reporting directly to Google CEO Sundar Pichai and overseeing Gemini model development, frontier AI research, and the Gemini app and developer teams. He replaces cofounder and CEO Demis Hassabis in this role, with Hassabis becoming the organization's chair. The move comes as Google tries to close the gap with OpenAI and Anthropic, which have outpaced Google's Gemini releases in 2026, and follows reports that Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed to improve coding performance.

events.headline: Anthropic to embed machine-readable watermarks in Claude AI outputs from August 2, 2026 to comply with EU AI Act
events.detail: Anthropic announced that all Claude products released from 2 August 2026 onward will include machine-readable marking in AI-generated content, with older models to be updated by 2 December 2026. The move is to comply with Article 50(2) of the EU AI Act, which requires providers to mark synthetic content as machine-readable and detectable. Anthropic said the watermark will be invisible, appearing either in text output or in metadata for audio, image, or video files, and will roll out globally, not just in the EU.

events.headline: Anthropic's Claude suffers major outage affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code and Claude Cowork.
events.detail: The outage began around 21:58 UTC on August 16, 2026, when Anthropic reported authentication issues affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. At 22:07 UTC, Anthropic reported degraded performance also affecting platform.claude.com. Users experienced login failures, loading errors, and incomplete requests. By 22:40 UTC, Anthropic confirmed all services were restored.

events.headline: Amazon and Nvidia expand AWS partnership with 2 million additional Nvidia GPUs for 2027-2028
events.detail: Amazon and Nvidia announced Wednesday an expanded deal adding 2 million more Nvidia GPUs, including Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra chips, to AWS data centers starting in Q3 and continuing through 2027-2028. This follows a March deal for over 1 million GPUs, with Nvidia citing demand that 'has exceeded expectations.' The deal also includes integration of Nvidia's networking hardware, CPUs, open models, and robotics platform (Omniverse, Cosmos, Isaac, Jetson) across AWS.

events.headline: US urges deregulation while EU enforces AI Act at G20 innovation ministerial in Chapel Hill
events.detail: At a G20 'innovation' ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina on September 1, 2026, US tech adviser Michael Kratsios pushed the 'Carolina Principles' against technology-specific regulation, joined by Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and Tesla's Elon Musk arguing for fewer AI constraints. The same day, the European Commission confirmed it sent information requests to more than 30 AI companies worldwide as a preliminary step toward possible investigations under the EU AI Act, focusing on safety and copyright compliance. Commission VP Henna Virkkunen, who attended the meeting, said Brussels is 'ready to take all necessary steps' to enforce the law.

events.headline: Cognition AI is set to raise about $1 billion at a $47 billion valuation.
events.detail: AI coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is close to finalizing a new funding round that would value it at roughly $47 billion. The company is raising around $1 billion, though the final size may exceed that given investor demand. Cognition reportedly received nearly $10 billion in investor interest for the round, according to people familiar with the matter.

events.headline: Meta agrees to $18 billion youth-safety settlement with 29 state attorneys general
events.detail: Meta settled with 29 U.S. state attorneys general after going to trial in August over claims Instagram and Facebook design features harmed younger users. Meta agreed to core platform changes for under-18 users, including a two-hour daily usage limit, disabling extreme makeup/cosmetic surgery filters, and tighter age verification. Meta will pay the $18 billion settlement over ten years and is booking a $10 billion legal charge in Q3. Payment in full is conditioned on rivals YouTube and TikTok making similar changes for younger users.
